Vietsovpetro JV Announces Major Investment to Boost Oil Production Capacity

Vietnam's leading oil and gas joint venture, Vietsovpetro JV, has unveiled a significant investment initiative aimed at expanding its offshore production capabilities in the Ba Ria–Vung Tau region. The move comes amid steady demand for crude oil and ongoing efforts to strengthen Vietnam’s energy sector.

Company executives confirmed on Thursday that the joint venture will allocate approximately $200 million over the next two years for the deployment of new drilling platforms and state-of-the-art extraction technology in the White Tiger oil field. This investment is expected to increase the field’s daily output by up to 10%, contributing an estimated 1.2 million additional barrels annually.

Pham Hoang Linh, General Director of Vietsovpetro JV, stated, “This expansion reflects our commitment to sustainable growth and supporting Vietnam’s long-term energy security. By modernizing our facilities and embracing advanced technologies, we aim to maximize recovery rates while adhering to the highest environmental standards.”

Vietsovpetro JV, a flagship collaboration between Vietnamese and international partners, has been a mainstay of Vietnam’s oil and gas sector since its establishment. The company currently accounts for nearly one-third of the nation’s crude oil output, with the Ba Ria–Vung Tau region serving as its operational core.

Analysts view the new investment as a positive signal for the industry. Nguyen Thanh Son, an energy sector analyst at Indochina Energy Research, commented, “Vietsovpetro JV’s decision to expand comes at a time when stable global oil prices and a supportive regulatory framework in Vietnam are encouraging upstream activity. This move will not only enhance local production but also help maintain the competitiveness of the country's oil exports.”

Vietnam’s Ministry of Industry and Trade welcomed the announcement, highlighting the broader impact on job creation and technology transfer. “Investments like these foster local expertise and support auxiliary industries in the region,” said Deputy Minister Tran Thi Mai.

Construction of the new platforms is set to begin in the third quarter of this year, with first oil expected by mid-2026. Local contractors, including the engineering firm Hoang Gia Petro, are slated to participate in the project, reinforcing the government’s emphasis on domestic industrial development.

Shares in Vietsovpetro JV’s partner companies rose modestly on Thursday following the news, reflecting cautious optimism among investors.
